plans.title: Show a real delivery date on every product, and price shipping into it
plans.summary: Every product page says **Delivery 3–5 working days** and every checkout adds a flat **4.95** for shipping, whatever the product, the warehouse or the country. The real date is only known after the order is captured and Fulfilment has allocated it. This plan computes a **delivery promise** per product and region in Fulfilment, carries it through the catalogue, pricing and search into the product page, cart, checkout and the financing quote, keeps it on the order, and tells the shopper when it slips.

plans.title: Let business customers add a VAT number and print it on the invoice
plans.summary: Business customers (clubs, schools, outdoor guides) cannot give us a VAT number at checkout. Billing adds it by hand after an email, re-issues the invoice PDF, and the first invoice stays wrong in the customer's inbox.

plans.title: Reserve stock at checkout so we stop selling what we don't have
plans.summary: Stock is only taken when a warehouse allocates the order, minutes to hours after the shopper paid. Two shoppers can buy the last tent; one of them is cancelled the next morning. This plan reserves stock for fifteen minutes when the shopper reaches payment, and turns the reservation into an allocation at capture.

plans.title: Show the delivery promise through the graph
plans.summary: The product page is one GraphQL operation, **ProductPage**. Three subgraphs answer it through the gateway, and the edge keeps each answer for ten minutes, so 92 % of product-page requests never reach the gateway. Fulfilment now computes the delivery promise ([[sch:delivery-promise]]). It is per region and moves with stock, yet the page still shows the static `leadTimeDays` from the catalogue. This plan adds a **promise subgraph** and a `Product.deliveryPromise` field, and splits the page: ProductPage stays as it is, and a new **ProductPromise** operation carries the promise. ProductPromise is public, has the region in its edge key and lives for 60 seconds. In the same window the price moves to a new pricing subgraph with a progressive `@override`, and `leadTimeDays` is removed.
